## Overview

Adyen authorization adjustment is an online-payments flow for changing the reserved amount on an eligible pre-authorized card or Klarna payment before final capture. It applies only to supported payment methods and Merchant Category Codes, depends on issuer acceptance, and is limited to payments acquired by Adyen.

## Lifecycle

The merchant pre-authorizes the payment, submits amount updates against the original payment PSP reference, and manually captures after the final intended adjustment. Asynchronous adjustment and capture outcomes are established through webhook events; a request response with a received state is not final outcome evidence.

Synchronous card adjustment requires account enablement and successive use of the latest `adjustAuthorisationData` blob. Klarna supports only asynchronous authorization adjustment and performs another risk assessment or credit lookup when the amount increases.

## Constraints

- Each update expresses the new total authorized amount rather than only the increment.
- Zero-value adjustments are not allowed, and a payment permits at most 50 adjustments; later adjustment requests are declined while capture remains possible up to the last successfully authorized amount.
- Pre-authorizations expire according to scheme validity. Extension uses an amount update equal to the current authorized balance and remains issuer-dependent.
- Capture is asynchronous, so merchants must finish all intended adjustments before starting capture and use webhook outcomes as the authoritative result.
